title: Monitoring Setup
description: Design a production monitoring stack using Linux-native tools, Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting best practices.

data.text: Monitoring tells you whether your system is healthy before users notice something is wrong. A well-designed monitoring setup combines metrics collection, visualization, and alerting into a single workflow that any team member can operate.
This lesson focuses on open-source tools that run naturally on Linux: Prometheus for metrics, Grafana for dashboards, and Alertmanager for notifications.
Metrics are numeric measurements such as CPU usage, request latency, or queue depth. Dashboards visualize those metrics. Alerts notify you when metrics cross a threshold.

items: Collect metrics with exporters that expose HTTP endpoints
Scrape endpoints on a schedule using Prometheus
Query and visualize data in Grafana
Route alerts to email, Slack, or PagerDuty via Alertmanager

data.title: Prometheus scrape configuration
data.code:
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'linux-node'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9100']  # node_exporter
    scrape_interval: 15s
    scrape_timeout: 10s

data.text: Google's Site Reliability Workbook recommends four golden signals for monitoring: latency, traffic, errors, and saturation. If you can see all four on a single dashboard, you can usually diagnose problems quickly.

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Alert on symptoms, not causes. Instead of alerting when CPU is high, alert when users see slow responses. This reduces noise and helps on-call engineers react faster.

data.title: PromQL: high error rate alert
data.code:
groups:
- name: app-alerts
  rules:
  - alert: HighErrorRate
    expr: rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) > 0.05
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "High error rate detected"
      description: "{{ $value }} errors per second"

data.text: Good alerts are actionable, specific, and graded by severity. A page-worthy alert should wake someone up. A ticket-worthy alert can wait until business hours.

items: Define severity levels: page, warn, and info
Include runbook links in alert annotations
Group related alerts to reduce notification noise
Test alerts with the on-call team during business hours
Review and tune alert rules monthly

data.title: Summary
data.text: Monitoring setup is not just dashboards. It is a feedback loop: collect metrics, visualize trends, and alert on symptoms. Use Prometheus and Grafana on Linux, follow the four golden signals, and design alerts that on-call engineers can act on immediately.
